note: Build a complete blend-oriented separation train to establish revenue, purities, and the cost of each branch.
notebook:

Starting with moderate stages/reflux and low pressure drops. Blends avoid expensive close-boiling individual C3-C6 separations; all three heavy components are worth recovering. Seven columns total.

note: Replace the failed train with a focused three-column backbone targeting the high-value C6 paraffin blend, using a stronger C5/C6 root split.
notebook:

The initial seven-column train failed at the feed; use fewer columns and a higher root pressure drop. C6 paraffins are the largest prize (~$1.15B/yr as a blend). A strong root boil-up is needed to keep C5 out of that blend. The C6/C7 split is easy; n-hexane/methylcyclopentane is close and needs a taller, higher-reflux column.

note: Push the nearly qualifying C6-paraffin cut above 95% to establish revenue before reducing the backbone cost.

Internal-flow balance for T indicates reflux 4 and boil-up 6 should send roughly 860 mol/s C3/C4 overhead and 695 mol/s C5 to bottoms. C5 blend revenue should be about $600M/yr. notebook: PLAN: Establish the first profitable sale by tightening the existing C6-paraffin/naphthene split; then reduce root and C6-column duties and recover other products only where margins justify them. The root gives B a useful C6+ feed. Current BT is approximately 95% C6 paraffin and would earn about $812M/yr, versus total plant cost $521M/yr, so it is the fastest route to positive reward. Its contaminants are chiefly methylcyclopentane and cyclohexane. Increase B from 60/6/4 to 80/8/5 at unchanged pressure to move the cut sharper without changing the root yet.

note: Reduce the dominant root-column energy and stage cost while preserving the proven C6-paraffin branch.
notebook: PLAN: First optimise the profitable two-column C6-paraffin plant by reducing root energy and size while retaining BT purity; then test a C5 recovery branch if the root can keep C6 out of T. Step 1: root duty reduction. Current best is root 50/4/6 dp.3 plus B 80/8/5 dp.2: revenue 813.8, cost 569.3, reward .558. B at 70/7/4 earns less and saves too little (.527). Root boil-up 6 is expensive; peer data show boil-up 2.2 roughly halves root cost. Reducing root to 45 stages and boil-up 4.5 should save substantially, retain most C6 in B, and may reduce DMB losses overhead. Watch BT C5 contamination and revenue; revert if it falls below spec.

note: Restore the island-best C6 backbone and modestly increase B boil-up to test whether additional paraffin recovery remains profitable without breaking blend purity.
notebook: PLAN: Optimise the proven two-column C6-paraffin plant, first B recovery then root energy. Copy R375 (reward .686) and test B boil-up 6.5.
